title: Data Validation
content:
Photon advocates for a Zero-Shim validation strategy. By integrating Zod directly into the execution path, we achieve type-safe contracts with zero runtime overhead.

Validation Philosophy

Data integrity is the first line of defense. Photon's architecture treats validation as a pre-flight operation that guards the handler from inconsistent state.

TYPE_INFERENCE

Schemas serve as the single source of truth, automatically generating TypeScript interfaces for your business logic.

PRE_COMPILED

Define schemas at the module level to ensure JIT-compilation happens once, eliminating per-request overhead.

ASYNC_REFINEMENT

Perform database existence checks and deep validation asynchronously without blocking the event loop.

Implementation Strategy

For maximum performance, decouple your validation contracts from the transport layer. This allows for schema reuse across REST, WebSockets, and internal service calls.

// 1. Module-Level Schema Matrix
const UserProfile = z.object({
  email: z.string().email(),
  tier: z.enum(['FREE', 'GOLD', 'ELITE'])
})

// 2. Fail-Fast Execution
app.post('/api/profile', async (c) => {
  const result = UserProfile.safeParse(await c.req.json())
  
  if (!result.success) return c.json({ 
    status: 'VAL_ERROR', 
    errors: result.error.flatten() 
  }, 422)
  
  const { email, tier } = result.data // 100% Type-Safe
  return c.json({ status: 'OK' })
})

// PROTOCOL_ADVISORY: JIT_OPTIMIZATION

Never define schemas inside the request scope. Schemas initialized within a handler are re-compiled on every request, leading to measurable latency spikes under high load.

Performance Benchmark

Comparing validation overhead: Static Schema Definition vs. Inline Dynamic Definition (100k requests).

MODULE_LEVEL_SCHEMA (STABLE) 0.012ms AVG
INLINE_DYNAMIC_SCHEMA (FRAGMENTED) 0.280ms AVG

// RECOMMENDATION: ALWAYS EXPORT SCHEMAS FROM DEDICATED MODULES

Advanced Pattern: Request Transformation

Validation isn't just about checking; it's about cleaning. Use Zod transforms to sanitize incoming data (e.g., trimming whitespace or coercing types).

const SearchParams = z.object({
  page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).default(1),
  limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).default(20),
  q: z.string().trim().min(2)
})

app.get('/search', (c) => {
  const result = SearchParams.safeParse(c.req.query())
  if (!result.success) return c.json(result.error, 400)
  
  const { q, page } = result.data // Sanitized and Typed
})

Pro Tip: When using @gravito/core, consider creating FormRequest classes. They combine authorization and validation into a single, testable entity that keeps your controllers purely focused on orchestration.
